results.summary: SoilZ v1 is a 1-bit IQ lock-in sigma-delta impedance analyzer for soil moisture sensing, implemented in IHP SG13G2 130nm BiCMOS. It uses a PTAT current source, H-bridge excitation, chopper demodulation, a continuous-time sigma-delta modulator, and a digital divider chain to produce a bitstream whose density is proportional to the impedance between two analog pins. The design is tested by connecting a resistive load or soil probe between ua[0] and ua[1] and counting the bitstream density with an external microcontroller such as an ESP32. Notable features include a 5-stage ring VCO with PTAT bias for temperature compensation and a programmable current source, but no silicon test results are provided.

LoRa Edge SoC is a RISC-V (RV32EC) system-on-chip based on the TinyQV bit-serial CPU, integrating peripherals such as CRC16, I2C master, SPI master, watchdog timer, RTC, and a tamper-detection register. It is designed for low-power edge applications and includes a radio interface for LoRa communication. The SoC is intended to be used with external memory and sensors via its I2C and SPI interfaces. No silicon test results are provided.

TinyMOA is a RISC-V CPU based on TinyQV with an integrated SRAM-based compute-in-memory accelerator for analog matrix multiplications. It is designed for edge AI inference, combining a bit-serial processor with analog MAC operations. The accelerator uses SRAM cells for analog computation, and the CPU controls data flow and results. No silicon test results are provided.

The design is intended to mimic moving a cursor on a screen, and no testing or silicon results are documented. It likely generates VGA signals to display a cursor on a monitor. The design uses a signal generator to produce the cursor movement pattern. External hardware would include a VGA monitor.
